hypothesis: Adding an explicit hinge on the upper-tier macro COUNT ratio and macro AREA ratio (only when macros exist) keeps the raw partition macro-balanced so the official repair step flips fewer macro nodes and preserves the learned cut structure.
analysis: Hypothesis partly held: repair_flips fell on all circuits (103→71, 238→207, 353→295) and cut/wcut improved on C1/C3, but C2 worsened (cut 318→334, wcut 1007→1097) and crit_cross rose everywhere (C1 0.011→0.093). Yet scores are negative on all circuits (total −0.719), so macro-balance gains did not translate to timing; the crit_cross increase plausibly offsets fewer flips. Seed spread is high (std 0.333; C2/C3 per-seed range ~0.6–0.9), unacceptable. Next: gate the hinge weight per-circuit or add a crit_cross penalty, and re-test with more seeds.
